newsitem.title: USA: New issues darlings of US corporate debt markets.
newsitem.headline: New issues darlings of US corporate debt markets.

text.p: New corporate debt dominated the session for both high-grade and junk markets on Friday with prices in both handily outperforming U.S. Treasuries, traders said.

Significantly tighter spreads for Norfolk Southern Corp's $4.3 billion eight-tranche deal sparked moderately heavy trade when the deal freed Friday morning, traders said. Much of the activity was generated by hedge funds with large positions that had foreseen an easy gain, they added.
Tranches of 20-, 30- and 100-year debt performed best, trading about six basis points tighter than original spread.

But for all the success of the deal, judged to be the largest investment grade issue in history, some traders also noted the size of the deal dictated it be priced to sell and bonds on Friday were finding equilibrium with actual market levels.
"When accounts see a deal that size they line up because they realize it's going to be on the cheap side," one trader at a West Coast firm said.
Elsewhere in high-grades, CIGNA Corp issued $600 million in debt, split evenly between 10- and 30-year tranches, to yield 77 and 97 basis points over the Treasury curve.
CIGNA's bonds priced on the wider side of price talk that was bandied about on Thursday. The deal priced via lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co.
Also on Friday, Chase Manhattan Corp issued $300 million in 10-year debt to yield 62 basis points over Treasuries via a Chase Securities syndicate.

Other secondary trade was light with spreads unchanged to firmer in spots, traders said. Still, some market participants said retail buying was lackluster ahead of the Federal Reserve policy-setting meeting next week.

Turning to high-yields, the fifth consecutive week of junk bond mutual fund cash inflows underpinned the market, traders there said. Inflows from funds that report on a weekly basis totaled $371.3 million in the week ended May 14, according to AMG Data Services in Arcata, Calif.
New issues reflected the firm tone -- some upsized and most trading significantly higher when freed to trade.

Issuance featured $175 million 10-1/4 percent 10-year debt from B3/single-B rated AFC Enterprises Inc (America's Favorite Chicken) via Goldman Sachs. The debt, which priced at par, traded up to 101 in late afternoon action.

Windy Hill Pet Food Co Inc upsized its 9-3/4 percent 144A B3/B-minus senior subordinated note deal from $100 million to $120 million before pricing through a Chase syndicate, sources said. The debt was seen trading in a 101-1/8 bid, 101-1/2 offer market late in the session.

Wiser Oil Co, an oil and gas producer and wholesaler in the U.S. and Canada, sold $100 million in 144A 9-1/2 percent 10-year B2/B-minus debt to yield 287.5 basis points over the curve through Salomon Brothers.

In contrast, U.S. Treasuries ended lower on Friday following a report that said housing starts rose 2.6 percent in April to 1.473 million annualized rate. But the masses were said on the sidelines ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.
Analysts said the market is uncertain as to whether the Fed would raise the Federal funds rate up another 25 basis points or leave it at the current level of 5-1/2 percent.
The 30-year Treasury bond closed down 15/32 at 96-15/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
